title: Camp Quartermaster
summary: The one who stayed at camp so the others could leave it.

title: Expedition Member
summary: You — one of the party that reopened the meadow.

title: The Twin-Strike
summary: The apex of the unaligned wilds; the meadow's first true wall.

title: The Broker
summary: Gildmark's hidden hand — the ledger says nothing was ever his doing, and the ledger is never wrong.

title: The Iron Regent
summary: Power that calls itself protection — the War-Countess's brother, seizing more emergency power than Embervale ever voted him.

title: The Bell-Keeper
summary: Every mis-rung bell is a father's love, paid to Gildmark in his daughter's name.

title: The Widow of the First Caravan
summary: She knew who lit the wagons before the ash cooled. It changed nothing she wants done.

title: The Ash Prophet
summary: A Cindervast deserter who preaches that everything standing is a lie waiting to fall.

title: The War-Countess
summary: Embervale's ruler, grieving and cornered by her own brother's ambition.

title: The Speaker of Norhollow
summary: Norhollow's veteran Speaker, who counts the dead before she answers anything.

title: The Elder of Rooktide
summary: Rooktide's elder, proof a town can come back if anyone's still willing to try.

title: Farrow the Forward
summary: A scout who goes first so the rest of the line doesn't have to.

title: The Clerk of Gildmark
summary: The whistleblower who priced his silence, then changed his mind, then paid for it in a different coin than he asked for.

title: The Thornveil War-Speaker
summary: A Thornveil voice at the truce table, killed to keep the ledger quiet.

title: Warden Bright
summary: A bell-warden who still believes the bell is meant to tell the truth.

title: Mirelle
summary: The Bell-Keeper's daughter, held as collateral for every proclamation he sealed false to keep her safe.

title: Liss of Embervale
summary: Writes letters across the line to a boy in Norhollow — the war was supposed to make them strangers.

title: Joren of Norhollow
summary: Reads every letter that reaches him, even the ones opened first by someone else's hands.
